findings.statement: CA9 is the most strongly induced tumour product with protein confirmation: RNA rises in paired tumour vs normal [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312] and protein follows [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]. The RNA change grows rather than shrinks when extrapolated to a pure tumour, so it is tumour-cell signal, not infiltration [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787].

NNMT protein is up in tumours [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], the RNA increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC paired samples [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.685] and higher expression goes with worse overall survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], making it one of the few candidates that is both up-regulated and prognostic.

PSAT1 tops the biomarker profile as a loss: RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.867] and protein [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963] both fall in tumours, yet within tumours the Cox model ties its residual expression to worse survival in TCGA-KIRC [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.43]. It is a prognostic and grading biomarker, not a target.

SCARB1, first in the target profile, is up at protein level [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.837] and the RNA increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=SCARB1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.989]; it is not prognostic.

SLC16A3 (MCT4, the lactate exporter) protein is up [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.279]; its S436 phosphosite rises in bulk but is slightly negative once adjusted for protein abundance [gene=SLC16A3; type=phosphosite_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; protein_adjusted_log2fc=-0.607], so the phospho signal reflects more protein, not extra phosphorylation.

ALDH6A1 loss has a real dosage component: copy number tracks its own RNA [gene=ALDH6A1; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=14q; rna_rho=0.525], and lower expression goes with worse survival in TCGA-KIRC [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554], a favourable-prognosis biomarker of retained tubule metabolism.

VHL is the disease mechanism: its chromosome arm is lost in most tumours [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=0.791] and it is the most recurrent somatic driver [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483]; the hypoxia programme it releases explains CA9, NDUFA4L2 and CD70 induction.

PBRM1 is the second recurrent driver [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362] and its copy-number loss lowers its own RNA [gene=PBRM1; type=cis_dosage; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; rna_rho=0.714], a true dosage effect of the arm loss rather than a passenger event.

FCER1G looks tumour-up in bulk but its expression falls steeply with tumour purity [gene=FCER1G; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_purity_rho=-0.692], so the signal comes from infiltrating myeloid cells rather than tumour cells.

RPS6KB1 (S6K1, downstream of mTOR) is the most activated kinase in tumours after adjusting phosphosites for protein abundance [gene=RPS6KB1; type=kinase_activity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; ksea_z=3.289], consistent with mTOR pathway activity in ccRCC.

NDUFA4L2 (COXFA4L2) has the largest protein increase of the leading candidates [gene=COXFA4L2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=3.768], a hypoxia-driven mitochondrial protein that is intracellular and has no tractable clinical drug of its own.

PCK1, a gluconeogenic proximal-tubule enzyme, is lost at protein level [gene=PCK1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.859]; like ALDOB and G6PC1 it marks loss of tubule identity and is a biomarker, not a target.

CD70 is up in tumour RNA [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.464] and protein [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421], a coherent surface-antigen profile.

ENPP3 protein is up in tumours [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544], a smaller change than CA9 or CD70 for a known antibody-drug-conjugate target.

The literature supports CA9 as both biomarker and imaging target: it is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low background in normal kidney, and CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept non-invasive discrimination of ccRCC that still needs prospective validation (PMID 42473996).

High CA9-targeted PET uptake is associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function alterations, immune pathway suppression with reduced B cell infiltration and enhanced angiogenic activity (PMID 42473996), linking the imaging signal to tumour genotype.

CD70 is reported as commonly overexpressed in renal cell carcinoma and minimally expressed in normal tissue, making it a potential therapeutic target (PMID 38195301); CD70-specific single-domain antibodies RCCB3 and RCCB6 have been labelled for PET radiotracers (PMID 39510586).

CD70 expression correlates with hypoxia pathway proteins, consistent with being a downstream target of hypoxia-inducible factor (PMID 38195301), and is associated with differentiation, metastasis and overall survival in a retrospective RCC series (PMID 39510586).

NNMT is reported as upregulated in ccRCC tumour tissue, with high expression correlating with worse overall and disease-specific survival, and is proposed as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target (PMID 41399267, a single study).
Potent and selective small-molecule NNMT inhibitors (II559, II802) have been described (PMID 37523719), so chemical matter exists even though no clinical NNMT drug is recorded.

NDUFA4L2 is overexpressed in most ccRCCs and contributes to proliferation and survival (PMID 36722045); HIF-1alpha induces it (PMID 42331208), and it suppresses mitochondria-associated ferroptosis together with LDHB, proposed as a combination target with radiotherapy (PMID 42331208).

ALDOB protein is diminished in ccRCC relative to adjacent normal tissue by IHC and is described as a prognostic biomarker (PMID 40852386, PMID 38655323); its proposed role as an immunotherapy target rests on bioinformatic associations with infiltrating Treg, Th17 cells and neutrophils.

One study reports that SLC16A3-mediated lactate export drives immune evasion in ccRCC through a GPR81-ERK-MYC loop, promoting M2 macrophage polarisation and suppressing CD8 T-cell function (PMID 42028950).

SLC6A19, a tubule amino-acid transporter lost in tumours, is reported to inhibit invasion and proliferation of ccRCC cells in experiments and to correlate with fatty acid metabolism and CPT1A (PMID 40099255), a tumour-suppressive, biomarker-type role.

FCER1G positively relates to macrophage infiltration and unfavourable prognosis, and combining it with CD68 has been proposed as a postoperative prognostic index (PMID 35120484), in line with its infiltration-driven bulk signal.

In the abstract corpus PSAT1 appears in a bioinformatic analysis where it is positively enriched in oncogenic signalling, glycolysis and cholesterol homeostasis (PMID 41971124); the corpus has no validated clinical study of PSAT1 despite its top data-driven biomarker rank.

PPP1R1A is a well-supported data candidate with no literature relations in the corpus: its loss replicates strongly in TCGA-KIRC [gene=PPP1R1A; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-5.179], a gap between the data and published work.

EPAS1 (HIF2A) is the established hypoxia target: strongly associated with ccRCC in Open Targets [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871] with the approved inhibitor BELZUTIFAN (APPROVAL). In DepMap ccRCC lines lean towards dependence [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3] without reaching significance [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.061].

The HIF inhibitor PT-2385 is not significantly ccRCC-selective in PRISM [gene=EPAS1; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.232], as expected because two-dimensional cell lines miss HIF-2 biology; this is a limitation of the screen, not evidence against the target.

KDR (VEGFR2) is the most drugged ccRCC pathway target, with approved agents including AXITINIB, CABOZANTINIB S-MALATE and TIVOZANIB (APPROVAL) and broad small-molecule and antibody tractability; it acts on tumour vasculature.

CA9 has a moderate Open Targets association with ccRCC [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088], antibody tractability and clinical agents including GIRENTUXIMAB and its iodine-labelled imaging form; in PRISM the most selective CA9-annotated compound is not significant [gene=CA9; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.146].
CD70 is antibody-tractable at advanced clinical level, with CUSATUZUMAB (PHASE_2) and the conjugate VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN (PHASE_1) among its agents; no approved drug yet.
ENPP3 is antibody-tractable with the conjugate AGS-16C3F (PHASE_2), and also has small-molecule ligands, but no approved drug.

SCARB1 (scavenger receptor B1, the HDL receptor) is a cell-membrane protein with a genetic-plus-literature Open Targets association [gene=SCARB1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4049] but no clinical drug: tractable but untested in ccRCC.
UniProt places SLC16A3 (a monocarboxylate transporter) at the basolateral and plasma membrane, where it dominates L-lactate efflux from glycolytic cells, an accessible but drug-less transporter.

NNMT is not a dependency of ccRCC lines in DepMap [gene=NNMT; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.316], so its target case rests on the tumour microenvironment and metabolism rather than cell-autonomous essentiality.

CCND1 is a strong dependency in ccRCC lines [gene=CCND1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-1.229] but not a selective one [gene=CCND1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.36]; no candidate in the top rankings is a selective ccRCC dependency.

SCD, a lipid-synthesis enzyme in the target profile, is a borderline dependency in ccRCC lines [gene=SCD; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=-0.501] that is not ccRCC-selective [gene=SCD; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; padj=0.771].

VHL is the top Open Targets ccRCC association [gene=VHL; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.6466], followed by the chromatin genes PBRM1, KDM5C, BAP1 and SETD2: genetic drivers that are not themselves druggable.

CA9 is tumour-intrinsic: ccRCC tumour cells carry nearly all its tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976] and about half of them express it [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=54.7%].

In Visium sections CA9 spot expression is explained by tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; composition_corrected_share=0.999], and its high-expression spots sit among other tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381] with only a slight macrophage enrichment.

KDR is an endothelial, not a tumour-cell, target: endothelial cells carry almost all its tumour transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951].

In situ, KDR spot expression is attributed to endothelium [gene=KDR; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=Endothelial; composition_corrected_share=0.99], and its high spots are enriched for endothelial and tumour-cell neighbours, the vascular niche that anti-angiogenic drugs act on.

CD74 is an antigen-presenting-cell gene: macrophages hold the largest share of its tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436], with dendritic cells expressing it most per cell, so it is a microenvironment target.

CXCR4 is a lymphocyte gene in ccRCC: most CD4 T cells express it [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD4_T; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=87.8%], together with B cells, so it is not a tumour-cell target.

SCARB1 is not cleanly tumour-intrinsic: tumour cells [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.336] and macrophages [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.384] share its transcripts, and endothelial cells express it most per cell [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; cpm_share=0.406].

EPAS1 transcripts in the tumour are spread across cell types, with endothelial cells holding the largest single share [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365]; its target value comes from HIF-2 protein stabilisation in tumour cells, which RNA cannot show.

The CA9 AlphaFold model is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; its top detected cavity is small [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8], and detected cavities recover half of the experimental ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. These describe a predicted monomer, not a degron or degrader site.

KDR has one of the highest descriptive structural-context scores [gene=KDR; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.841], at its kinase-domain cavity; this heuristic reflects model confidence, cavity geometry and nearby lysines and does not predict degradability.

COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is the leading tumour-track discovery candidate: tumour cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], the increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.829] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It is not prognostic [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.123], is not a DepMap dependency, has never been seen at the cell surface by mass spectrometry and lacks normal-tissue staining data.

RAB42, a little-studied small GTPase, is the second tumour-track candidate: tumour cells carry most of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], the rise replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and holds at purity one [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189]. It is intracellular, so not antibody-accessible, is not prognostic or a dependency, and was not measured in the confirmatory cohort.

OLFML2A, a secreted matrix protein, leads the stroma track: fibroblasts make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647], the increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=OLFML2A; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.372] and persists at purity one [gene=OLFML2A; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527]; it is not a dependency and lacks confirmatory-cohort data.

COX4I2, a hypoxia-linked cytochrome oxidase subunit, is a stroma-track candidate made mostly by fibroblasts and pericyte-like cells [gene=COX4I2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.893] whose increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COX4I2; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.139]; it is intracellular and expressed in lung, which weakens it as an antibody target.

MILR1, a macrophage surface receptor with no ccRCC papers, tops the immune track: macrophages make most of its transcripts [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.841], the rise replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=MILR1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=2.436] and goes with worse survival [gene=MILR1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.343], but it almost vanishes in a pure tumour [gene=MILR1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414]: an infiltration-driven signal.

LILRB4, an inhibitory myeloid receptor, is made almost only by macrophages [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.933]; its increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=LILRB4; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.7] but shrinks towards zero in a pure tumour [gene=LILRB4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508], so it measures myeloid infiltration and is a microenvironment hypothesis.

In IMmotion150 higher CD70 is associated with longer progression-free benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383], not significant after correction [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166], and it does not separate the combination from sunitinib [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.934].

Higher CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib in IMmotion150 [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], an association that does not survive correction [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332].

In CheckMate 025 NNMT shows no association with progression on nivolumab [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=0.083] after correction [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.padj=0.88]; its prognostic value does not translate into a treatment-response signal.

CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup candidate: higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in CPTAC RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971] and TCGA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148], and lower in the ccB subtype [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-1.551].

PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours in TCGA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] and in the aggressive ccB subtype [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364], which fits its adverse prognostic association; the BAP1 shift is not confirmed at protein level.

SLC16A3 does not differ by PBRM1 status at protein level [gene=SLC16A3; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.631] nor by ccA/ccB: a pan-ccRCC rather than subgroup candidate.

CD70 has one of the best antibody-drug-conjugate profiles [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]: surface protein, no vital-organ enrichment in the GTEx proteome, but heterogeneous, with a minority of tumour cells expressing it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%]; staining data are missing.

CA9, a known radioligand target used as a control, scores well for conjugates [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647] with no kidney staining, but its protein is enriched in stomach [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19], an on-target off-tumour risk.

ENPP3, a control with a clinical conjugate, has a moderate suitability score [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578], held back by high staining in normal kidney and duodenum despite confirmed cell-surface detection.

COL23A1 ranks among the top conjugate candidates [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.705] with a large extracellular domain and no vital-organ protein enrichment, but few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.5%] and staining data are unavailable.

SCARB1 is a weak conjugate candidate: its protein is enriched in adrenal gland [gene=SCARB1; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.08] and few tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%].

MILR1 is an immune-cell gene [gene=MILR1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.995] that tracks M2 macrophages across tumours [gene=MILR1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_m2_macrophages=0.586], so it marks immunosuppressive myeloid-rich (hot) tumours.

The checkpoint control PDCD1 behaves as expected, tracking CD8 T-cell infiltration closely [gene=PDCD1; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.811], which calibrates the immune profiles of the candidates.

LILRB4 follows the overall immune score very closely [gene=LILRB4; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.853], a marker of hot, myeloid-rich tumours rather than a tumour-cell target.

The CD70 cell attribution is dataset-dependent: in Li 2022 tumour cells hold a minority of its transcripts [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.345] with T/NK cells dominant, whereas in Zhang 2021 tumour cells dominate [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.964]; the immune profile also attributes a large share to immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654].

SCARB1 attribution also disagrees between datasets: myeloid cells dominate in Li 2022, while in Zhang 2021 tumour cells hold the larger share [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582], so its tumour-intrinsic status is uncertain.

The tumour-cell origin of COL23A1 replicates in a second single-cell dataset, where tumour cells again dominate [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.941].

HK2 does not replicate in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort: the protein change there is slightly negative [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256] and not significant [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074], despite a strong increase in the discovery cohort.

NNMT protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort with the same direction and strong significance [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776].

PSAT1 protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946], although its one shared phosphosite does not.

SLC16A3 protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551], and so does its shared phosphosite.

caveats: Single-analyst run: the work of five specialists was done by one agent with fewer tool calls per layer, so coverage of each layer is narrower than in the multi-agent arm.
CA9, COL23A1, RAB42 and OLFML2A were not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort (too sparse there); this is missing data, not a failure to replicate.
Single-cell attribution of CD70 and SCARB1 differs between Li 2022 and Zhang 2021; tumour-intrinsic calls for these genes are uncertain.
No candidate in the rankings is a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap; two-dimensional cell lines also miss HIF-2 biology.
Treatment-response results are single-gene associations from small trial arms; no gene separates the trial arms after correction.
Literature support is limited to the ingested abstract corpus; absence of relations does not mean absence of published work.
Structural-context scores describe predicted monomer cavities and do not identify degrons or predict degradation.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; novelty is counted by gene-symbol literature volume.
